concepts.def: Turning effect of a force about a point: moment = force × perpendicular distance from pivot. Units: Nm.
Body in equilibrium if resultant force = 0 AND resultant moment about any point = 0.
For equilibrium, sum of clockwise moments = sum of anticlockwise moments about same point.
Point where weight of a body acts. For uniform rod, lies at midpoint. For composite shapes, use moments to find it.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Moments — a core area of A-Level Maths.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Moments brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Moments.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: A force of 10 N acts perpendicular to a rod, 0.5 m from the pivot. Moment is:
options: 5 Nm
20 Nm

mcqs.q: For a body in equilibrium, the sum of moments about any point is:
options: zero
positive
equal to weight × distance
depends on pivot

mcqs.q: What is the derivative of a constant, like d/dx(5)?
options: 0 — constants do not change with x.
The derivative of 5 is 1 because all constants differentiate to 1.
The derivative of 5 is 5 because the constant stays the same.
180 degrees, the same as a triangle.

mcqs.q: What is the sum of the interior angles of any pentagon?
options: 180 degrees, the same as a triangle.
360 degrees, because all polygons' angles sum to one full turn.
540 degrees — use (n - 2) x 180 with n = 5.
It is reflected in the y-axis because of the minus.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Reaction at a support”?
options: Point where weight of a body acts. For uniform rod, lies at midpoint. For composite shapes, use moments to find it.
Beams on supports: each support provides a normal reaction. Use moments and force balance to find magnitudes.
Beam about to tip when reaction at one support becomes zero. Useful for limit-case problems.
Turning effect of a force about a point: moment = force × perpendicular distance from pivot. Units: Nm.

For equilibrium, sum of clockwise moments = sum of anticlockwise moments about same point.
